candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is cystic lymphangioma, a benign lymphatic vascular malformation. MCN is a mucinous epithelial neoplasm with malignant potential. While both can appear as well-circumscribed cystic masses in the pancreatic head and share some clinical overlap (female predominance, large size, normal CA 19-9 possible), they are histologically and biologically distinct entities. The thrombocytosis and elevated BUN in this case, along with the absence of pancreatitis history and the specific clinical features, point toward lymphangioma rather than MCN. MCN is a related but incompatible subtype within the differential of pancreatic cystic lesions.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: MCN is a distinct pancreatic cystic neoplasm (epithelial, mucin-producing, ovarian-type stroma) versus cystic lymphangioma which is a benign lymphatic malformation; both can present as large cystic pancreatic head masses in middle-aged women but they are different diagnostic entities with different histogenesis

case_quality_flags: Thrombocytosis >1,000,000/µL and elevated BUN are atypical features for both MCN and cystic lymphangioma; thrombocytosis may be reactive or represent essential thrombocytosis as a coincidental finding
Cystic lymphangioma of the pancreas is rare; diagnosis typically requires histopathology (endothelial lining, lymphatic channels) not available in this record
Normal CA 19-9 slightly favors non-mucinous etiology but does not exclude MCN
